tagline: Two miles of old turnpike above a drowned valley.
intro: Route 53 crosses from Weston into Redding and runs two miles to where Route 107 joins it, on the line of the Norwalk and Newtown Turnpike, a private turnpike organized in 1829. The old turnpike followed this road from Norwalk as far as the Saugatuck Reservoir, then kept straight on toward Newtown by roads the towns look after now.
Redding lies across three ridges running north and south, with steep valleys between. Its lowest ground, about 290 feet, is at the reservoir.

moments.title: Saugatuck Reservoir
moments.text: The water company flooded the Saugatuck River valley for it, taking the villages of Hull and Valley Forge, and finished the dam in January 1942.

moments.title: Saugatuck River
moments.text: Where the scenic stretch ends, Route 107 comes in and the two roads cross the Saugatuck together, a little under a mile west of Redding Center.
